title: Beef Burger
subtitle: Homemade beef patty with the lot
excerpt: A hand-formed beef patty made with well-seasoned coarse-ground beef, cooked in a hot pan until charred on the outside and juicy within. Served in a toasted brioche bun with the classic toppings.

recipe.sourceNotes: The hamburger takes its name from Hamburg, Germany, where minced beef steaks were a common preparation in the 19th century. American cooks developed the fried or grilled burger in a bun, and it became a global fast-food and home-cooking staple. The home-made version is far better than any commercial equivalent. Fat content matters: 15 to 20% fat keeps the patty juicy. Do not press the patty while cooking: pressing squeezes out the fat and dries the burger.

recipeTools.notes: Or a griddle pan for char marks.

content.text: Handle the mince as little as possible: overworking compresses the proteins and makes the burger dense. A dimple pressed in the centre of each patty stops it puffing up like a ball as it cooks. Get the pan very hot before the patties go in. Do not press them down during cooking.
Divide the mince into 4 equal portions. Shape each loosely into a patty about 2 cm thick. Press a shallow dimple in the centre with your thumb. Season generously on both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat a large frying pan or griddle pan over very high heat until smoking. Add a little oil. Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium, or 4 to 5 minutes per side for well done. Do not press down. If adding cheese, place a slice on each patty in the last minute and cover with a lid to melt.
Toast the cut sides of the brioche buns in the pan for 1 minute. Assemble with lettuce, tomato, onion rings, gherkins, and the burger patty. Serve immediately.
